options.description: Print JSON instead of a table

notes: --json prints {"schema", "ok", "checks": [{"label", "status", "hint"}], "services": [...]}; status is pass, fail or warn. warn means flk works but an optional feature (port forwarding) is off; ok is false only when a check fails.

commands.name: version
commands.summary: Print the flk version

commands.name: resume
commands.summary: Start every machine that should be running (after a reboot, or after stop-all)
notes: Should be running: started, restarted, deployed or scaled, and not stopped with `flk machine stop` since. A machine whose app exited counts too.
flk-machines.service runs it at boot (sudo /home/dayne/flk/setup-host.sh --install-service).
-a APP limits it to one app.

commands.name: stop-all
commands.summary: Gracefully stop every running machine, remembering to resume them
notes: What the host does at shutdown (flk-machines.service): all machines stop in parallel, each with its kill_timeout, and `flk resume` brings them back.
To stop a machine for good, use `flk machine stop`.
-a APP limits it to one app.

commands.name: launch
commands.usage: flk launch [--name NAME] [--image IMAGE] [--port PORT] [--cpus N] [--memory MB] [--no-deploy]
commands.summary: Create flk.toml (if missing) in the current directory, register the app, deploy

options.description: App name (default: directory name)
Use a prebuilt image instead of a Dockerfile
internal_port in the generated flk.toml (default 8080)
vCPUs in the generated flk.toml (default 1)
Memory in the generated flk.toml (default 256)
Register the app but don't deploy

notes: An existing flk.toml or fly.toml is used as-is; the options only shape a new one.
Deploys right away unless --no-deploy, or there's no Dockerfile / [build] image yet.

commands.name: deploy
commands.summary: Build the image and roll machines to a new release

options.description: Deploy this image instead of building
Leave a machine that fails its health checks on the new release (to debug it)

notes: Reads flk.toml / fly.toml in the current directory, or with -a APP the file flk recorded at the app's last launch/deploy, so it works from anywhere.
Creates machines on the first deploy (count from `flk scale count`, default 1); later deploys stop, update and reboot each machine in turn.

With health checks ([checks], services tcp_checks/http_checks, http_service checks; type tcp, http, or flk's log), each machine must pass them before the next is updated. One that fails goes back to its previous release, the release is marked failed, and the deploy stops (exit 1).
Without checks it waits up to 30s per machine for internal_port to accept connections, then warns but carries on.
Warns about flk.toml keys it doesn't know (typos).
Volumes named in [[mounts]] must exist first: flk volumes create NAME --size 1 (one per machine).

subcommands.name: rollback
subcommands.summary: Roll machines back to an older release's image and config (default: the one before the current)

options.description: If the old release fails its health checks, leave the machine on it
Also put the volumes back as they were on that release (from the backups [flk.backup] before_deploy took when leaving it)

notes: Makes a new release (vN+1) from the old one, without building, and rolls it out like a deploy, health checks included.
If deploy --no-rollback left machines on a failed release, the default is the current (last good) release instead.
--with-volumes needs a before-deploy backup of every volume, taken when the machines left that release (see [flk.backup] before_deploy). The volumes' current data is backed up first, then replaced.
Only releases whose image is still kept can be used: the last two by default ([flk] keep_releases = N keeps more).
Volumes aren't touched unless --with-volumes; otherwise restore data with flk volumes restore.

commands.name: logs
commands.summary: Serial console output (app stdout/stderr and boot messages)

options.description: One machine (default: all)
Lines of history (default 50)
Keep following, even without a terminal
Print and exit, even in a terminal

notes: Follows new output only when stdout is a terminal; piped or run by an agent it prints the last lines and exits.
Each machine keeps console.log, rotated to console.log.1 past FLK_LOG_MAX_MB (default 10) MB.

commands.name: console
commands.summary: Attach to a machine's serial console, or --send one line to the app's stdin

options.description: Type one line into the app's stdin, then return (no terminal needed)
With --send: print console output until a line matches REGEX
With --wait-log: give up after this long (default 10)

commands.blocks: attaches an interactive terminal; agents: use --send (and --wait-log), or `flk logs`
notes: Detach with Ctrl-b d (Ctrl-b Ctrl-b d inside tmux). Attaching needs a terminal; --send doesn't.

--send types TEXT and Enter into the app's stdin (needs [flk] stdin = "console", the default). With --wait-log it then prints the console output until a line matches REGEX (exit 1 after --timeout). The console echoes what you type; that echo is skipped when matching.
It's the serial console, not a shell: you see app output and type to its stdin (server consoles: stop, say, op...). Ctrl-C here doesn't signal the app; use flk machine stop.
For a shell in the machine, use flk ssh console; to run a command, flk exec.

commands.name: exec
commands.usage: flk exec CMD... [--instance ID] [--user USER] [--cwd DIR] [--tty] [--stdin] [--timeout SECONDS]
commands.summary: Run a command in a running machine and return its output and exit status

options.description: Which machine (default: the app's first running one)
Run as this user: a name, UID or UID:GID (default: root)
Working directory (default /)
Give it a terminal (needs one here): for interactive programs
Pass this command's stdin to it (default: its stdin is empty)
Kill it after this long (exit status 124)

notes: Put -- before the command when it has options of its own: flk exec -- ls -la /data. stdout and stderr stay apart, and flk exits with the command's status. No terminal needed.
It runs beside the app (not as its child), with the app's environment, as root unless --user. Ctrl-C is passed on to the command.
Needs the flk agent in the machine: releases built since flk had exec include it (building it needs Go; see flk doctor).

commands.name: ssh
commands.summary: A shell in a running machine: flk ssh console

subcommands.name: console
subcommands.usage: flk ssh console [ID] [--command CMD] [--user USER] [--send TEXT] [--wait-log REGEX] [--timeout SECONDS]
subcommands.summary: An interactive shell in a machine (like fly ssh console); -C runs one command

options.description: Run CMD (through sh -c) instead of an interactive shell
As this user (default: root)
Type one line into the app's stdin, then return (no terminal needed)
With --send: print console output until a line matches REGEX
With --wait-log: give up after this long (default 10)

subcommands.blocks: an interactive shell needs a terminal; agents: use -C CMD or flk exec
notes: The shell is bash if the image has it, else sh. Without -C it needs a terminal here.
--send/--wait-log type into the app's stdin over the serial console, as with flk console (kept for scripts that used flk ssh console as an alias of it).

commands.summary: Forward a local TCP port to a machine

commands.name: events
commands.summary: What happened to apps and machines: starts, stops, exits, deploys, checks, backups, ports

options.description: Every app (default: the app here or -a APP; every app when there's none)
Keep printing new events until interrupted
From this time on: ISO (2026-10-13T12:00:00Z) or a duration back (30s, 10m, 2h, 3d)
How many recent events (default 50; with --since, all since then)
Print JSON instead of a table

notes: --json prints one object per line: { at, app, machine, type, release?, detail? }; at is UTC with milliseconds, and --since TIME includes events at TIME (so a reconnecting reader may see one twice).

Types: machine.created, machine.started, machine.updated, machine.restarted, machine.stopped, machine.exited, machine.gave_up, machine.rolled_back, machine.paused, machine.resumed, machine.destroyed, check.passed, check.failed, deploy.started, deploy.succeeded, deploy.failed, backup.succeeded, backup.failed, backup.copied, backup.copy_failed, volume.restored, port.forwarded, port.dropped. The full list with meanings is in flk help --all.
Kept in STATE/events.jsonl (rotated at 4MB to events.jsonl.1). --follow blocks by design; stop it with Ctrl-C.

commands.name: files
commands.summary: Files inside a volume (or a backup of one): list, read, copy in and out; no mount, no root
notes: VOL:PATH names a path in volume VOL (its name or ID); PATH is absolute inside it, default /. Built on debugfs (e2fsprogs).

Reading works any time: on a running machine's volume it shows what's on disk, which can lag a little; --backup reads a backup instead. Writing (cp into a volume, rm, mkdir, chown) needs its machine stopped, and ends with an e2fsck of the volume.

subcommands.name: ls
subcommands.usage: flk files ls VOL[:PATH] [--to DIR] [--backup BACKUP] [--json]
subcommands.summary: List a directory in a volume

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Read a backup of VOL instead (latest, or part of its name)
Print JSON instead of a table

notes: --json: [{ name, type (file, dir, symlink, other), size, uid, gid, mode ("0644"), mtime (to the minute) }].

subcommands.name: cat
subcommands.usage: flk files cat VOL:PATH [--to DIR] [--backup BACKUP]
subcommands.summary: Print a file from a volume

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Read a backup of VOL instead

subcommands.name: cp
subcommands.usage: flk files cp SRC DST [--to DIR] [--backup BACKUP] [--owner UID[:GID]]
subcommands.summary: Copy a file or directory into or out of a volume (one side is VOL:PATH)

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
When copying out: read a backup of VOL instead
When copying in: owner of the new files (default: the target directory's owner)

notes: Like cp -r: into an existing directory it goes inside it; a file in the volume is replaced. Modes come from the copied file (also when it replaces one: the local file's mode, not the old one's; chmod it first if needed); owners come from --owner or the directory copied into, not the host's user IDs.
Examples: flk files cp ./server.properties world:/ ; flk files cp world:/logs ./logs

subcommands.summary: Delete a file (or with -r, a directory) in a volume; its machine must be stopped

options.description: Delete a directory and everything in it

subcommands.summary: Make a directory in a volume; its machine must be stopped

options.description: Make missing parents too; no error if it exists
Owner (default: the parent directory's)

commands.name: volumes
commands.summary: Persistent disks (sparse ext4), one machine each

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.summary: Volumes and what they're attached to

options.description: Print JSON instead of a table

subcommands.name: create
subcommands.usage: flk volumes create NAME [--size GB] [--path FILE] [--from-dir DIR]
subcommands.summary: Create a volume for [[mounts]] source = NAME

options.description: Size in GB (default 1)
Create the image at FILE (e.g. on a bigger disk) instead of flk's state dir; flk never deletes it
Fill it with a copy of DIR (owner/group IDs kept as-is)

subcommands.name: import
subcommands.summary: Register an existing ext4 image as a volume; flk never deletes it

options.description: An existing ext4 image file (required)

notes: Size comes from the file. Don't mount it on the host while a machine uses it.

subcommands.name: destroy
subcommands.summary: Delete an unattached volume and its data (external volumes: unregister, keep the file)

options.description: Also delete an external (--path / import) volume's file

subcommands.name: backup
subcommands.usage: flk volumes backup [ID|NAME...] [--to DIR] [--keep N] [--mode MODE] [--no-check] [--no-copy]
subcommands.summary: Copy volumes (default: all of the app's) to the backup dir, then prune old copies

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Keep this many backups per volume (default: [flk.backup] keep, host backup_keep, 7)
stop, live or pause: override [flk.backup] mode
Skip the e2fsck of the copy
Don't copy it to backup_copy_to (host.toml) this time

notes: How the app is kept from writing comes from [flk.backup] in flk.toml (see flk help --all): by default its machine is stopped for the copy and started again; mode = "live" with pre/post hooks (e.g. save-off / save-on) copies while it runs.
Copies are sparse, and instant on XFS/btrfs when the backup dir shares the volume's filesystem. The copy is checked with e2fsck (a copy of a running machine gets its journal replayed).
With backup_copy_to in ~/.config/flk/host.toml, the new backup is then copied there too (see flk volumes copy); a failed copy makes the command fail, but the backup is kept.

subcommands.name: copy
subcommands.usage: flk volumes copy [ID|NAME...] [--to DIR] [--dest DEST] [--backup BACKUP] [--keep N]
subcommands.summary: Copy backups to another disk or host (off this machine), then prune old copies there

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Where to: a dir (another disk) or HOST:DIR (rsync over ssh) (default: backup_copy_to in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Which backup (default: the latest)
Copies kept at DEST per volume (default: backup_copy_keep, else backup_keep, 7)

notes: Copies go to DEST/APP/VOLUME/, like the backup dir. Ones already there are skipped, so it's safe to rerun. Remote copies use rsync over ssh with keys (BatchMode: no password prompts), resume when cut off, and run at idle I/O priority.
Each backup records its copies (copies in flk volumes backups --json); flk doctor warns when the newest copy is older than backup_copy_warn_days (8).

subcommands.name: backups
subcommands.summary: List a volume's backups (default: all of the app's volumes), newest first

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Print JSON instead of a table

subcommands.name: restore
subcommands.usage: flk volumes restore ID|NAME [BACKUP] [--to DIR] [--as NEW] [--path FILE]
subcommands.summary: Replace a volume's data with a backup (default: the latest); its machine must be stopped

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Restore into a new volume NEW instead (no stop, the volume is untouched); names are lowercase letters, digits and underscores (e.g. world_restored)
With --as: create the new volume's image at FILE (flk never deletes it)

notes: BACKUP is a file name from flk volumes backups, or part of it (e.g. its date). The current image is kept beside it as FILE.before-restore-TIME, not deleted.

--as NEW copies the backup into a new, unattached volume while everything keeps running: to test a restore, look inside (debugfs), or mount it in another app. NAME may be a volume that's gone (its backups remain). If NEW is a [[mounts]] source, the next machine that needs one may attach it.

subcommands.name: verify
subcommands.summary: Check backups without changing them: e2fsck -n, then the [flk.backup] verify hook

options.description: Backup dir (default: backup_dir in ~/.config/flk/host.toml)
Which backup (default: the latest); part of its file name works
Every backup of each volume
Print JSON instead of a table

notes: The hook is a host command run in the flk.toml's directory with FLK_BACKUP (the image file), FLK_APP and FLK_VOLUME; exit 0 means good. It can read files with debugfs, e.g. debugfs -R 'stat /world/level.dat' "$FLK_BACKUP". flk volumes backup runs it too, after its own check.
The result is kept with the backup (verify, verified_at in flk volumes backups --json). Exits 1 when any backup isn't clean.

subcommands.name: move
subcommands.usage: flk volumes move ID|NAME [--dir DIR] [--path FILE]
subcommands.summary: Move a volume's image file to another directory or disk; its machine must be stopped

options.description: Move the image into DIR (e.g. a bigger disk, or XFS for instant backups)
Move it to exactly FILE

notes: A sparse copy, checked with e2fsck, then the volume points at it. The old file is deleted if it was in flk's state dir; an external one (--path / import) is kept for you to delete.
Moving into flk's state dir makes it an ordinary volume again. On another disk, the boot service must start after that disk is mounted (flk prints what to do if not).

subcommands.name: extend
subcommands.summary: Grow a volume and its filesystem; its machine must be stopped

options.description: New size in GB (required; grow only)
